explain.say: In an earthquake the ground jerks quickly back and forth. A normal building is fixed to the ground, so all that shaking goes straight up into it.

explain.say: A stiff base slab above the bearings ties the building together so it moves as one block. Many bearings also have a lead core that soaks up energy, and a gap around the building gives it room to drift.

faq.a: Engineers make them strong and flexible, with steel or reinforced concrete that bends without snapping, bracing or shear walls, and sometimes base isolation or dampers to reduce the shaking that reaches them.

Base isolation separates a building from the ground with flexible bearings, usually layers of rubber and steel. The ground shakes underneath while the building above moves much more slowly and gently.
asks: Why do buildings sit on rubber pads?

faq.q: Why do isolators have rubber and steel layers?
faq.a: Thin steel plates stop the rubber bulging, so the bearing is stiff up and down and can carry the weight, while the rubber still lets it move easily sideways.
asks: How does a rubber bearing carry a building?
What is a lead rubber bearing?

faq.q: Does a base-isolated building still move?
faq.a: Yes, it drifts sideways as a whole, sometimes by tens of centimetres, which is why a gap is left around it. But it moves slowly and smoothly, so there is far less damage inside.
asks: What is the gap around an isolated building for?

faq.q: Why are hospitals often base isolated?
faq.a: Hospitals must keep working straight after an earthquake. Isolation protects not just the structure but the equipment, pipes and people inside from violent shaking.

facts: Lead rubber bearings, invented in New Zealand in the 1970s, combine rubber and steel layers with a lead core that absorbs energy.
Base isolation makes a building sway much more slowly, moving it away from the fast shaking typical of most earthquakes.

quiz.why: Soft sideways, the bearings let the ground shake beneath while the building above moves slowly and gently.

wrong.1: They add little weight; their job is flexibility.
wrong.2: Rigid fixing is what a normal building has; isolation does the opposite.
